samples.summary: `removeLink`'s new selection branch snapshots and writes even when the selection contains no hyperlink, contradicting its documented no-op
samples.evidence: `if (selection.hasSelection() && selection.range) { applyStyleImpl({ href: undefined }); return; }` (text-box-editor.ts:1254-1257) is taken for *any* selection. `applyStyleImpl` (line 823) unconditionally calls `docStore.snapshot()` and `doc.applyInlineStyle(range, {href: undefined})`, then `requestRender()` / `notifyStyleApplied()`. The caret branch below it correctly bails via `if (!link) return`, and both the interface doc (`text-box-editor.ts:311` "No-op when neither finds one") and the shared `TextFormattingEditor.removeLink` doc (`packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/types.ts:101`) promise a no-op. The new toolbar button is deliberately always enabled (`text-format-group.tsx:168-178`, "`removeLink()` is a no-op off a link, so an over-eager click costs nothing"), so a click with an ordinary text selection is the normal case: it pushes an undo entry that changes nothing (the user's next Cmd+Z appears to do nothing) and dirties the text box for commit. A cheap guard would be to check the selection actually carries an href (e.g. `linkRunCoveringRange` / a run walk) before writing.

samples.summary: `pendingStyleFor` seeds only from the caret run style and discards any already-staged pending style except `href`, so consecutive collapsed-caret toolbar writes lose each other
samples.evidence: `const seed = { ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style };` (editor.ts:1191) — `getSelectionStyleImpl()` reads the *document* run style (`caretInlineStyle`) and never merges `pending.get()`, and `pending.set` replaces state (pending-style.ts:22-24). The very next lines do read `pending.get()` (line 1193) but only to look at `href`. Consequence on a collapsed caret: click Bold (pending = caretStyle+bold), then pick a colour → pending becomes caretStyle+colour and the staged bold is silently dropped, even though `getSelectionStyle` (editor.ts:3279-3285) and `getRangeStyleSummary` (3309-3315) *do* merge pending and therefore keep reporting bold on. The sibling seeds elsewhere deliberately merge pending first (`TextEditor.toggleStyle`, text-editor.ts:3466-3468; `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`, text-box-editor.ts:880-881), so the toolbar path is the odd one out. Pre-existing expression, but the diff rewrote exactly this seed and taught it to consult `prev` for one key only.

samples.summary: The extracted `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` drops the old `pos.offset > start` condition, widening the result for zero-length runs on every caller, not just Clear formatting
samples.evidence: The removed private method (text-editor.ts, old lines ~5899-5910) required `pos.offset === end && pos.offset > start`; the shared version keeps only `position.offset === end && inline.style.href` (caret-style.ts:90). That deliberately accepts the empty-href residue, but it also fires for a zero-length href inline sitting at any boundary — e.g. `[{'abc',{}}, {'',href:'x'}]` reports a trailing edge at offset 3, and `[{'',href:'x'}, …]` reports one at offset 0, positions where the caret is not after any linked *text*. The consumers are not only the new Clear-formatting paths: `TextEditor.exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` (text-editor.ts:5913) is reached from typing a space (981), Enter (2608/2641) and 4171, and it now stages `href: undefined` in those boundary cases. `normalizeInlines` (store/block-helpers.ts:89-112) drops empty inlines unless they are the sole one, so in the local store the reach is limited to the residue case; blocks coming from other producers (Yorkie tree materialisation, PPTX import) are what make this uncertain. Impact is a spurious pending write rather than data loss, hence minor.

samples.summary: Arming the link exit from `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` alone (not only from an already-armed exit) makes any collapsed-caret toolbar write break link continuation, diverging from plain typing and from the Cmd+B keyboard path
samples.evidence: `const exitsLink = isAtLinkTrailingEdge(doc, cursor.position) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined);` (editor.ts:1194-1196). The stated problem the guard exists for is that `pending.set` *replaces* an exit `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` already armed (editor.ts:1173-1176) — the second disjunct covers that. The first disjunct goes further: with the caret clicked at a link's end and no pending state (mousedown clears pending, text-editor.ts:1795), clicking Bold/a colour/a font-size step now stages `href: undefined`, so the continuation the user types is unlinked. Plain typing in that same position still extends the link (the char inherits the run's href), and so does the keyboard Cmd+B, because `TextEditor.toggleStyle` merges pending over the caret style instead (text-editor.ts:3465-3468, 3497) and therefore sees the run's own `href`. Toolbar and keyboard toggles now produce different link extents from the identical caret position.

mergedFrom.summary: Every other collapsed-caret style write in `EditorAPI` bypasses the new trailing-edge guard and re-arms the link
Only the trailing edge is guarded: at the *leading* edge of a link the toolbar clear seeds pending with the link's href and extends the link backwards

finding.summary: New link-trailing-edge guard is bolted onto `clearInlineFormatting` only; every other caller of `applyStyleImpl`'s collapsed-caret branch still re-arms the link from the caret style
finding.evidence: `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1170) stores `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)`. `getSelectionStyleImpl()` is the raw caret style, which at a link's trailing edge is the link run's style **including `href`**, and the prior pending state is NOT merged in — so any pending `href: undefined` armed by `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` is discarded. The diff patches only the `clearInlineFormatting` entry (editor.ts:3364-3372). The bypassing call sites are `applyStyle: applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:3342 — toolbar Bold/Italic/color/etc.) and `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`'s collapsed branch (editor.ts:1283). Concretely: click the caret at the end of a hyperlink (mousedown clears pending), click toolbar Bold, type a character — the pending style carries the link's `href`, so `consumeForInsert` writes it onto the new text and the hyperlink silently grows. That is exactly the failure mode the new override exists to prevent, reachable through the sibling toolbar buttons. (Pre-existing shape, but it is the path around the new guard.)

verdict.reason: The finding describes code that is not in this tree. `applyStyleImpl`'s collapsed-caret branch does not do `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)`; it calls `pending.set(pendingStyleFor(style), cursor.position)` (editor.ts:1203). `pendingStyleFor` (editor.ts:1190-1198) is the shared seed for EVERY collapsed-caret write and applies the link-exit rule itself: unless the incoming `style` names `href` (e.g. insertLink), it appends `href: undefined` when `isAtLinkTrailingEdge(doc, cursor.position)` is true, and it also preserves an already-armed pending `href: undefined` via the `prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined` clause — so the "prior pending state is NOT merged in" claim is false too. The two cited bypass paths both route through that seed: `applyStyle: applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:3375, toolbar Bold/colour) and `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`'s collapsed branch, which calls `applyStyleImpl({ fontSize: ... })` (editor.ts:1316). `clearInlineFormatting` (editor.ts:3377-3391) contains no special-case guard at all — it just calls `applyStyleImpl(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)`, with a comment stating the rule deliberately lives in `pendingStyleFor` instead. The lines the finding cites as the patched guard (editor.ts:3364-3372) are unrelated style-summary aggregation code. So the concrete scenario (caret at link trailing edge -> toolbar Bold -> type) hits the guard at editor.ts:1194-1197 and yields `href: undefined`.

finding.summary: Dropping `href` from CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE leaves an empty-inline href residue unclearable by any command
finding.evidence: `link-run.ts:27-31` documents that `normalizeInlines` leaves an `href` residue on a fully-emptied paragraph, and `findLinkRunAt` deliberately refuses to anchor on an empty-text inline (`inlines[i].text.length > 0` at link-run.ts:44). `removeLink` (editor.ts:3724, text-box-editor.ts:1237) is built on `findLinkRunAt`, so it no-ops on such a run. Until this change, Clear formatting was the one command that stripped that stale `href`; with `href` removed from `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` neither command touches it. Worse, on a collapsed caret in that paragraph `applyStyleImpl` (editor.ts:1170) stores `{ ...caretInlineStyle(...), ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }`, and `caretInlineStyle` has no residue guard (caret-style.ts:106-112), so the pending style now carries the residual `href` and the next typed characters become a hyperlink the user never created. `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` cannot help: an empty run fails its `position.offset > start` test.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism is contradicted by the code. (a) It claims `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` "cannot help: an empty run fails its position.offset > start test" — no such test exists; caret-style.ts:87-95 checks `position.offset === end && inline.style.href`, which is TRUE for a zero-length residue inline (end === 0 === offset, no following same-href inline), and caret-style.ts:61-69 documents that counting empty-text href runs is deliberate precisely to handle the `normalizeInlines` residue. (b) It claims `applyStyleImpl` stores `{ ...caretInlineStyle(...), ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE }` on a collapsed caret — it does not; editor.ts:1203 calls `pendingStyleFor`, which at editor.ts:1194-1197 adds `href: undefined` whenever `isAtLinkTrailingEdge` is true, so the pending style cannot carry the residual href and typed characters do not become a hyperlink. The Cmd+\ path has the same re-arm at text-editor.ts:3440-3448, and the slides `applyStyleImpl` (text-box-editor.ts:823-824) returns early with no selection so it never seeds a caret style at all. The `findLinkRunAt` empty-run refusal (link-run.ts:44) is real and the model-level residue does survive, but it is an invisible pre-existing `normalizeInlines` wart with no user-visible wrong behavior remaining once the seeding path is guarded — the claimed blocking harm is unreachable.
